 The public is encouraged to view the agenda and meeting at CityofVernon.org/publicmeetings. You
 may address the Commission in the Council Chambers, via mail or email to
 PublicComment@cityofvernon.org, include the meeting date and item number in the subject line
 (mail and/or email must be received at least two hours prior to the start of the meeting).

subject matter jurisdiction of the Commission. The public will also be given a chance to comment

Subject
Quarterly City Housing Report

Recommendation
Receive and file the 2024 Second Quarter City Housing Report.

Background
Staff will present the Quarterly City Housing report, for the period from March through May 2024.
The report highlights rent, occupancy, inspections, and repairs. In conjunction with the quarterly
update, City Staff will provide the Commission a summary of housing related inquiries.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

  6, 2023 Special Vernon Housing Commission Meeting Minutes.
3.  Permission for Absence
  Recommendation: Excuse Chair Juliet Goff from attending the March 13, 2024
  Regular Vernon Housing Commission Meeting.

 NEW BUSINESS

4.  Standard Residential Lease and Vernon Housing Commission Procedures

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report.

  In response to Commission questions, Public Works Director Wall and City
  Attorney Moussa explained the reasons for the revisions, applicable laws
  regarding criminal background checks and security measures related to new
  applicants for City owned rental stock.

MOTION
  Commissioner Froberg moved and Commissioner Ybarra seconded a motion to:
  A. Adopt the revised Standard Residential Lease and the following revised Vernon
  Housing Commission guiding procedures: 1) Lease Procedures for New Tenants;
  2) Appliances in City-owned Housing Units Procedures and 3) Occupant
  Relocation Procedures; and B. Adopt new Rental Rate Procedures. The question
  was called and the motion carried 5-0, Chair Goff and Commissioner Lopez
  absent.

Meeting Date:  June 12, 2024
From:  Deborah Harrington, Interim City Clerk
Department:  City Clerk
Submitted by:  Yonnie Parker, Deputy City Clerk

Subject
Housing Lottery for City-Owned Housing

Recommendation
Conduct housing lottery to establish randomized order to fill a City-owned housing vacancy at
3349 Fruitland Avenue (two-bedroom house).

Background
Pursuant to Vernon Housing Commission (VHC) policies and procedures, and to ensure that the
selection process for new tenants remains equitable and transparent, the City conducts a housing
lottery when a City- owned housing unit becomes available. A housing lottery will consist of two
randomized drawings from 1) all names on the Unit Transfer Request list; and 2) all names on
the Housing Interest list. The randomized drawings establish an order by which a vacancy shall
be offered. A compilation of VHC policies and procedures and housing lottery information are
available on the City’s website at www.cityofvernon.org/housing.

Currently, the City has the following vacancy that requires a lottery:
  • Two-bedroom house at 3349 Fruitland Avenue

Pursuant to the Lease Procedures for New Tenants Section 2, the Notice of Available Housing
was posted at City Hall on April 29, 2024; published in the Los Angeles Wave (Huntington Park
Bulletin) on May 2, 2024; widely publicized on the City’s website and social media outlets; and
advertised on Zillow (and Zillow affiliated websites) for 35 days. The online interest form
submission system has yielded a tremendous response.

Per the Lease Procedures for New Tenants Section 3 and Occupant Relocation Procedures
Section B, all Housing Interest Forms and Unit Transfer Request Forms received by June 5,
2024, are included in the lottery for the vacancy at 3349 Fruitland Avenue. One lottery will be
conducted at the VHC meeting scheduled for June 12, 2024.

 Forms Received by June 5, 2024  Quantity
 Unit Transfer Requests for 3349 Fruitland Avenue  2
 Housing Interest Forms for 3349 Fruitland Avenue  421

Housing Interest and Unit Transfer Request lists for the lottery are available online at:
www.cityofvernon.org/VernonHousingLottery.

Under the Occupant Relocation Procedures, priority for vacant units is given to existing tenants
who have submitted a Unit Transfer Request. Existing tenants of City-owned housing can
submit Unit Transfer Requests and are entered into a lottery following the provisions of the
Lease Procedures for New Tenants. If the transfer tenant either does not want to occupy the
vacant unit, or does not qualify for the vacant unit, then the vacant unit will be offered to the
next transfer tenant from the lottery results. If the vacant unit has been offered to all current
tenants with applicable Unit Transfer Requests and none of the tenants either wants to occupy

  Item 3  Page 13 of 23
 the vacant unit or qualifies for the vacant unit, then the vacancy will be offered to those on the
New Tenant Lease lottery selection.

Fiscal Impact
There is no fiscal impact associated with this report.

   CITY OF VERNON
  NOTICE OF AVAILABLE HOUSING

The City of Vernon has the following available housing unit for rent:

3349 Fruitland Avenue - 2 bedroom / 1 bathroom house - $2,000 per month

Pursuant to the City of Vernon Housing Commission Lease Procedures for New
Tenants, a lottery will be conducted on June 12, 2024, at 6:00 p.m. in the City Hall
Council Chambers.

Housing Interest and Unit Transfer Request Forms are available on the City’s website
at cityofvernon.org/vernonhousinglottery. To be entered in the June 12, 2024 lottery,
interest forms must be submitted online no later than June 5, 2024, 5:30 p.m. For
additional information, contact the Public Works Department at (323) 826-1472.

Additional information on  City-owned  housing  units  is  available  at
cityofvernon.org/cityhousing.

  MINUTES
  VERNON HOUSING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  WEDNESDAY, JUNE 12, 2024
  COUNCIL CHAMBER, 4305 SANTA FE AVENUE

  CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Nevarez called the meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.

  FLAG SALUTE

  Vice Chair Nevarez led the Flag Salute.

  ROLL CALL

  PRESENT:
  Juliet Goff, Chair (arrived at 6:10 p.m.)
  Jorge Nevarez, Jr., Vice Chair
  Steven Froberg, Commissioner
  Leticia Lopez, Commissioner
  Marlene Ybarra, Commissioner

  ABSENT:
  Ronit Edry, Commissioner
  Bertha Padilla, Commissioner

  STAFF PRESENT:
  Angela Kimmey, Deputy City Administrator
  Zaynah Moussa, City Attorney
  Deborah Harrington, Interim City Clerk
  Dan Wall, Public Works Director

  APPROVAL OF THE AGENDA

  Staff requested that New Business Item No. 3 be considered after Public
  Comment.

  MOTION
  Commissioner Lopez moved and Commissioner Ybarra seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda with New Business agenda item No.3 moved to be considered
  after Public Comments. The question was called and the motion carried 4-3, Chair
  Goff and Commissioners Edry and Padilla absent.

  Regular Vernon Housing Commission Meeting Minutes  Page 2 of 3
  June 12, 2024

  PUBLIC COMMENT

  None.

  Chair Goff arrived at 6:10 p.m. and relinquished the chair to Vice Chair Nevarez.

  NEW BUSINESS

  3.  Housing Lottery for City-Owned Housing

  Interim City Clerk Harrington presented the staff report and conducted the Housing
  lottery to establish the randomized order to fill the City-owned housing vacancy at
  3349 Fruitland Avenue (two-bedroom house).

  Staff conducted the randomized order of unit transfer list and new interest form list.

  PRESENTATIONS

  1.  Quarterly City Housing Report

  Public Works Director Wall presented the staff report and accompanying
  PowerPoint.

  In response to questions from Commissioners, Public Works Director explained
  the efforts of City Administration staff to reduce and soon eliminate the outstanding
  rent balances; and announced receipt of a formal application for permits from the
  property owner at 5201 S. Santa Fe to repurpose the existing building into 18
  apartments.

  MOTION
  Commissioner Froberg moved and Chair Goff seconded a motion to receive and
  file the 2024 Second Quarter City Housing Report. The question was called and
  the motion carried 5-2, Commissioners Edry and Padilla absent.

  CONSENT CALENDAR

  MOTION
  Commissioner Lopez moved and Commissioner Ybarra seconded a motion to
  approve the Consent Calendar. The question was called and the motion carried 4-
  1-2, Chair Goff abstained, Commissioners Edry and Padilla absent.

  The Consent Calendar consisted of the following item:

  2.  Meeting Minutes
  Recommendation: Approve the March 13, 2024 Regular Vernon Housing
  Commission Meeting Minutes.
